categories.extraction: How to extract structured information from raw input
categories.dedup_conflict: How to handle duplicates, contradictions, and updates
categories.storage_organization: Backend choices, data model, and memory organization
categories.retrieval_ranking: How to find, rank, and format relevant memories

techniques.name: Reflexion loop for extraction completeness
techniques.summary: After initial extraction, LLM self-checks for missed entities/facts and iterates up to 3 rounds. Improves recall at the cost of extra LLM calls.
techniques.tradeoffs: Higher recall; 2-3x LLM calls per extraction.
techniques.when_to_use: When extraction completeness is critical and LLM budget allows.

techniques.name: Tool executions as memory source
techniques.summary: Memorize what the agent did (tool I/O) instead of conversation. PostToolUse hook captures every tool execution; AI extracts structured observations.
techniques.tradeoffs: More actionable and less noisy than raw dialogue; only works for tool-heavy agents.
techniques.when_to_use: Tool-heavy coding agents where tool executions are the primary unit of work.

techniques.name: Multimodal message accumulation before extraction
techniques.summary: Batch heterogeneous inputs (screenshots, voice, text) until a threshold before sending to memory. Reduces API calls and improves context window usage.
techniques.tradeoffs: Adds latency (batching delay); requires threshold tuning.
techniques.when_to_use: Multimodal input scenarios where individual items are too small to extract from efficiently.

techniques.name: 8-category extraction with L0/L1/L2 output
techniques.summary: Extract memories into 8 categories (profile, preferences, entities, events, cases, patterns, tools, skills) with three-level output per memory: L0 abstract (~100 tokens), L1 overview (~2k tokens), L2 full content.
techniques.tradeoffs: Comprehensive but heavyweight; requires well-tuned category decision table.
techniques.when_to_use: Long-running agents accumulating diverse memory types across many sessions.

techniques.name: Tool/Skill memory with automatic statistics
techniques.summary: Track tool/skill usage metrics (call count, success rate, avg duration, tokens) from execution records; persist as structured memory with LLM-merged guidelines across sessions.
techniques.tradeoffs: Requires ToolCall/SkillCall record format in messages; adds per-tool storage overhead.
techniques.when_to_use: Tool-heavy agents where learning tool best practices across sessions matters.

techniques.name: Bi-temporal edge invalidation for contradiction handling
techniques.summary: Instead of deleting or overwriting old facts, set invalid_at timestamp and keep history. Supports point-in-time queries and audit trails.
techniques.tradeoffs: Requires graph DB with temporal fields; more complex queries; storage grows monotonically.
techniques.when_to_use: When facts evolve/contradict over time and temporal reasoning ("what was true at time T?") is needed.

techniques.name: Vector pre-filter + LLM dedup (skip/create/none)
techniques.summary: Two-phase dedup: vector search finds similar existing memories (same category + owner), then LLM decides skip/create/none with per-item merge/delete actions. Post-LLM normalization prevents contradictory action combinations.
techniques.tradeoffs: Precise but requires 1 LLM call per candidate; vector pre-filter keeps LLM calls manageable.
techniques.when_to_use: Any memory system needing structured dedup beyond simple exact-match.

techniques.name: Schema-driven graph via Pydantic ontology
techniques.summary: Define entity types and edge types as Pydantic models (entity_types, edge_types, edge_type_map). Ensures consistency and enables type-specific extraction prompts.
techniques.tradeoffs: Upfront schema design effort; less flexible for unstructured or evolving data.
techniques.when_to_use: When memory has well-defined entity types and relationships worth enforcing via schema.

techniques.name: Dedicated agent per memory type
techniques.summary: Each of 6 memory types has its own agent with own schema and tools. The agent decides what to extract and how to store it. More flexible than a single monolithic extraction step.
techniques.tradeoffs: High orchestration overhead (7+ agents); significant latency and cost per memory update.
techniques.when_to_use: When different memory types need fundamentally different storage/retrieval strategies.

techniques.name: Dual ownership for user vs agent memories
techniques.summary: User-space memories (profile, preferences, entities, events) and agent-space memories (cases, patterns, tools, skills) have separate storage, merge policies, and retrieval paths. Prevents cross-contamination.
techniques.tradeoffs: Requires ownership classification at extraction time; routing logic adds complexity.
techniques.when_to_use: When user facts and agent-learned knowledge should not mix in retrieval.

techniques.name: Progressive disclosure with token cost visibility
techniques.summary: Show a compact index first (ID, title, token cost); let the agent decide what to fetch in detail. ~10x token savings vs dumping full context.
techniques.tradeoffs: Requires two-step retrieval (index then fetch); agent must be capable of choosing.
techniques.when_to_use: When memory corpus is large and most entries are irrelevant to current query.

techniques.name: 3-layer retrieval: search, timeline, get_observations
techniques.summary: search (browse index) -> timeline (situate in temporal context) -> get_observations (full details). Each layer is independently useful; the agent stops drilling when satisfied.
techniques.tradeoffs: More round-trips; requires MCP or multi-step tool interface.
techniques.when_to_use: When memory has temporal structure and the agent benefits from progressive context loading.

techniques.name: Hierarchical directory-based retrieval with score propagation
techniques.summary: Organize memories in directories; retrieval explores high-scoring directories recursively. Child score = 0.5*embedding + 0.5*parent_score. Stops when top-k converges (unchanged for 3 rounds).
techniques.tradeoffs: Requires directory structure; more complex than flat vector search; convergence adds latency.
techniques.when_to_use: When memories have natural hierarchical organization (categories, subcategories).

techniques.name: L0/L1/L2 tiered representation per memory
techniques.summary: Each memory has three detail levels: L0 one-liner abstract (~100 tokens) for candidate selection, L1 structured overview (~2k tokens) for reranking, L2 full content on demand. Token cost scales with need.
techniques.tradeoffs: 3x storage per memory; extraction must produce all three levels.
techniques.when_to_use: Large memory corpora where full-content retrieval is too expensive for initial ranking.

techniques.name: Compressed state first, raw retrieval on demand
techniques.summary: Build a compressed state summary; only retrieve original raw chunks when the compressed state is insufficient. Reduces context size when the summary is enough.
techniques.tradeoffs: Lossy compression may miss details; sufficiency check adds one LLM call.
techniques.when_to_use: When a summary usually suffices and raw retrieval is the exception.

techniques.name: LLM sufficiency gates — retrieve only when needed
techniques.summary: Instead of always retrieving, ask LLM 'is this enough?' at each retrieval stage. SUFFICIENT skips retrieval; NEED_RETRIEVAL triggers the next stage. Avoids unnecessary retrieval cost.
techniques.tradeoffs: One LLM call per gate; may incorrectly judge sufficiency.
techniques.when_to_use: When retrieval is expensive and compressed/cached context often suffices.

techniques.name: Multiple specialized rerankers composed per search type
techniques.summary: Cross-encoder, node-distance, episode-mentions, MMR — each reranker captures a different relevance signal. Configurable per search type via SearchConfig.
techniques.tradeoffs: Each reranker adds latency; diminishing returns from stacking too many.
techniques.when_to_use: When single-signal ranking (e.g. vector similarity alone) is insufficient.

techniques.name: LLM relevance scoring per chunk (0-10)
techniques.summary: Score each trajectory chunk 0-10 for query relevance using LLM, select top-k. Alternative to vector similarity or BM25 when semantic judgment matters.
techniques.tradeoffs: One LLM call per chunk; expensive for large corpora; high quality for small sets.
techniques.when_to_use: When semantic relevance judgment matters more than speed, and candidate set is small.

techniques.name: Hotness-driven archival with automatic cold memory removal
techniques.summary: Score memories by sigmoid(log1p(access_count)) * exp(-decay * age_days). Memories with hotness < 0.1 and age > 7 days auto-archived to _archive/. Retrieval scope narrows naturally over time.
techniques.tradeoffs: Requires access counting; archived memories need explicit restoration if needed later.
techniques.when_to_use: Long-running agents with growing memory where natural pruning is preferred over manual cleanup.

techniques.name: Hierarchical chunk compression with state replacement
techniques.summary: Process trajectory chunks sequentially; each chunk's LLM compression replaces the previous accumulated state (not appends). Produces a single evolving summary that grows in quality, not size.
techniques.tradeoffs: Lossy; earlier details may be lost; requires sequential processing.
techniques.when_to_use: When a single evolving summary is preferred over append-style accumulation.

techniques.name: Meta Memory router with fixed evaluation order
techniques.summary: A single classification step routes incoming content to appropriate memory type handlers. Fixed evaluation order (Core -> Episodic -> Procedural -> Resource -> Knowledge Vault -> Semantic) avoids redundant processing.
techniques.tradeoffs: Router LLM call adds latency; fixed order may not suit all content distributions.
techniques.when_to_use: When memory has multiple types requiring different extraction/storage strategies.

techniques.name: Core memory as always-in-context blocks
techniques.summary: Persona and human blocks with character limits are always injected into the system prompt, not retrieved on demand. Guarantees identity and key user info are never missed.
techniques.tradeoffs: Consumes fixed context budget regardless of relevance; character limits constrain content.
techniques.when_to_use: When certain memory (identity, key preferences) must always be available regardless of query.

techniques.name: Community nodes for topic-level aggregation
techniques.summary: Cluster related entities via Label Propagation algorithm; LLM generates a summary for each cluster. Enables high-level 'tell me about topic X' queries without enumerating individual entities.
techniques.tradeoffs: Graph algorithm + LLM summarization per community; rebuild cost on graph changes.
techniques.when_to_use: When queries span multiple related entities and topic-level summaries are valuable.

techniques.name: Session lifecycle hooks for automatic memory capture
techniques.summary: Hook into session lifecycle events (SessionStart, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd) for automatic capture. No manual 'save' calls needed — memory extraction is triggered by events.
techniques.tradeoffs: Tightly coupled to host agent's plugin/hook system; requires compatible lifecycle API.
techniques.when_to_use: When the host agent has a plugin/hook system and memory should be captured automatically.

techniques.name: Two-file fact/event separation (always-in-context + grep-searchable)
techniques.summary: Split memory into two files: a facts file always injected into the system prompt, and an append-only event log searchable via grep. Facts are never missed; events don't bloat context.
techniques.tradeoffs: Facts file must fit in system prompt; no selective retrieval of facts; history search is keyword-only.
techniques.when_to_use: When fact volume is small enough to always fit in context and simplicity is preferred over retrieval sophistication.

techniques.name: Token-pressure-driven multi-round consolidation
techniques.summary: Consolidation triggers when actual prompt token estimate exceeds the context window. Loops up to 5 rounds, each time archiving a chunk at a user-turn boundary, targeting half the window as headroom. Token-based, not message-count-based.
techniques.tradeoffs: Requires token estimation (provider-native or tiktoken fallback); boundary selection adds logic.
techniques.when_to_use: Any agent needing predictable context window management with automatic headroom.

techniques.name: Grep-based history retrieval without vectors or embeddings
techniques.summary: Agent searches event history using shell grep commands. No vector store, no embeddings, no semantic search. Entries are timestamped and keyword-rich by design. An always-on skill teaches the agent grep patterns.
techniques.tradeoffs: Keyword-only; no fuzzy/semantic matching; requires agent to have shell exec capability.
techniques.when_to_use: When history entries are well-structured with timestamps/keywords and semantic search infrastructure is undesirable.

techniques.name: Hybrid retrieval pipeline: embedding similarity + BM25 keyword + reranker
techniques.summary: Standard two-stage retrieval: stage 1 runs embedding cosine similarity and BM25 keyword match in parallel, merges candidates via reciprocal rank fusion (RRF); stage 2 reranks the fused list with a cross-encoder or LLM scorer. Embedding handles paraphrase and semantic drift; BM25 catches exact terms the embedding may miss. The reranker corrects ordering errors from either channel.
techniques.tradeoffs: Requires an embedding API and a vector store (FAISS, Qdrant, ChromaDB, etc.); BM25 index adds a second storage path; reranker adds latency per query. Strong generalization — good default when query types are diverse.
techniques.when_to_use: Default retrieval choice when the environment supports embedding calls and the memory must handle varied query phrasings with high recall. Prefer simpler grep-based or pure-LLM scoring when embedding is unavailable or memory volume is very small.
